subject: Air-gapped VPC cluster footprint and disk failover plan

Subject: Air-gapped VPC cluster footprint and disk failover plan

Hi Ellen / BRMC infra team —

Thanks for the intake call this morning. Per our discussion, I put together a concise runbook of open items we need to finalize to produce the SOW and the cluster blueprint for your air-gapped VPC site. High-level asks below; please reply inline with clarifications so we can lock the plan by EOD Friday.

Quick summary of the constraints we captured:
- Fully air-gapped control plane (no outbound egress for cluster control traffic)
- On-site NFS for archival + local NVMe for model cache and runtime KV stores
- Backup traffic must be able to leave to your internal archival cluster (no public cloud transfer)

Open questions (please mark answers):
1) Desired retention window for model checkpoints and customer logs (RTO/RPO expectations).
2) Do you have a preferred blockstore/Cinder provider (Ceph/Rook or proprietary SAN)?
3) Preferred topology for disk failover — do we implement per-node NVMe mirroring (RAID1) + periodic snapshot to on-site blockstore, or local NVMe + host-initiated replication to SAN?
4) Expected sustained qps and peak token throughput per cluster (helps size node pools).

Proposed next steps from our side after we get answers:
- Finalize node-pool mix (control, inference, GPU burst, and infra) and sizing CSV.
- Storage class definitions: local-ssd (for KV/cache), blockstore-io (for persistent volumes), and archive-nfs (for long-term retention).
- Network zoning diagram and egress gating policy for vendor updates (OCI images and hotfixes staged via internal bastion).

I've attached a short worksheet (BRMC_Storage_Requirements.xlsx) and a first-pass network diagram (network-zones-v1.pdf).

If convenient, can we schedule a 30-min runthrough Thursday morning PST to walk the node sizing spreadsheet?

Thanks —
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Air-gapped VPC cluster footprint and disk failover plan

Sofia —

Thanks for the concise list. Quick answers below and a few clarifying follow-ups:

1) Retention: model checkpoints — 14 days hot, 90 days cold archive. Logs: 30 days searchable, 365 days cold storage (we only need immutable audit for compliance).
2) Blockstore: we have a Ceph-backed SAN in the data hall and a legacy NetApp array for archival. Primary preference is Ceph for PVs; archival can be NetApp/NFS.
3) Disk failover: Our internal ops prefers host-level NVMe for perf, with asynchronous replication to Ceph. RAID at host level is not standard for us — we rely on Ceph for durability. If that's incompatible with Redwood assumptions, tell us the trade-offs.
4) Throughput: baseline inference is expected at 250 tok/s sustained, burst to 1.2k tok/s for 30-90s windows. Concurrency: ~20 steady inference workers, up to 80 during peaks.

Other notes:
- Patching/upgrades: because the cluster is air-gapped we will provide a secure internal image registry. Plan needs to include an image staging workflow and signed image verification.
- Compliance: we require FIPS-validated crypto on control-plane certificates.

We are available for the Thursday slot; prefer 10:00–10:30 PT.

—Ellen
Dr. Ellen Park
CTO, Blue Ridge Medical Center
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Air-gapped VPC cluster footprint and disk failover plan

Ellen / team —

Thanks for the answers, that helps a lot. Based on your retention and throughput targets, here is the initial technical proposal (summary):

Node pools (first-pass):
- control-plane (3x m6-standard equivalent, 16 vCPU, 64GB RAM) — HA etcd + kube-controller-manager internal-only.
- infra (2x m6-standard, 8 vCPU, 32GB) — csi provisioner, registry mirror, audit/elastic forwarder.
- inference-gpu (NVIDIA A40 equivalent) — fleet scaled by GPU count, expected base 4 GPUs, burst to 12 GPUs during peak windows; keep node-local NVMe per GPU node for model shard cache.
- cpu-worker (16x c6-standard equivalent) — for small tasks, batching agents, and sidecar workloads.

Storage recommendation:
- local-ssd (StorageClass: local-ssd, reclaim: Delete): ephemeral NVMe for model KV cache and local runtime. Volumes sized per GPU node: 1–2TB NVMe depending on model weight.
- blockstore-io (StorageClass: ceph-rbd, reclaim: Retain): Ceph-backed PV for persistent KV snapshots and smaller model artifacts (RWO).
- archive-nfs (StorageClass: nfs, reclaim: Retain): NetApp-backed NFS for cold archive (immutable snapshots) and audit logs.

Failover approach:
- Don’t RAID the NVMe at host-level. Use local NVMe for hot cache + periodic snapshot to Ceph (every 10–15 minutes for checkpoint metadata; full model snapshot on deploy).
- For critical replicated state (etcd, Redis-like KV), use Ceph-backed persistent volumes placed on the infra node-pool with anti-affinity rules.

Networking / airgap specifics:
- Image delivery via internal registry mirror hosted in the infra pool; images signed and verified on node boot.
- Egress: control-plane management will run through a bastion jump in BRMC VLAN A; we will provide an ops runbook for manual image staging and emergency hotfix paths.

Action items for BRMC to confirm (short):
- Confirm NVMe sizing per GPU node (1TB vs 2TB).
- Confirm Ceph RBD IO profile (ssd-hdd mix).

I attached a CSV (redwood-nodegrid-sizing.csv) with the initial node counts and expected throughput estimates. I’ll incorporate Ellen’s retention numbers into the snapshot cadence in that file.

-Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Ellen / infra team —

Appreciate the quick turn. Confirming next steps after our call this morning:

1) BRMC to drop signed images tarball + internal registry endpoint in Drive folder: https://drive.redwood.internal/BRMC/airgap-preflight (expected by Mon 11/23 COB).
2) BRMC to confirm NVMe per GPU node: Decision: 2TB NVMe (Sofia note: >1TB recommended for current models).
3) Redwood to produce SOW draft and acceptance criteria (target for initial draft: Tue 11/24 EOD). SOW will include: preflight checklist, test acceptance (smoke + perf), patching workflow, and the image staging process.
4) Storage: final design will use Ceph-RBD for durable PVs and NetApp NFS for cold archive; we will not require host-level RAID on NVMe — we’ll snapshot to Ceph every 15 minutes for metadata and do nightly full model checkpoint push to archive-nfs.

If that aligns, Marissa will kick off SOW document and Irene will assemble the operations runbook (image staging, signed verification steps, and bastion procedures).

Forwarding the drive link and SOW doc link back once the draft is ready.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to the call notes and the signed-image tarball.

-Sofia
